Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

fade verb

lose colour, strength or freshness

also faded, fade (of a colour), lose colour, wither (of flowers), lose its bloom, fade out

classical

Lucr. 2.828: ēvānēscere stinguīque colōrem (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Div. 2.117: dē vīnō aut salsāmentō putēs loquī, quae ēvānēscunt vetustāte

ēvānēscō, ēvānēscere, ēvānuī

verb, third conjugation

fade away, lose strength, die away

Of a colour, a smell, wine that goes flat, a sound or a memory (memoria … obscūrāta est et ēvānuit, Cic. de Or. 2.95). It is also the word for vanish (see disappear).

Other words

  • pallēscō, pallēscere, palluī — grow pale; of leaves, fade

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ov. Ars 3.704: pallēscunt frondēs (Lewis & Short); Gell. 19.4.4 (Lewis & Short)

    First of people who turn pale with fear or worry; of leaves and of a flame, losing their colour.

  • marcēscō, marcēscere — wither, droop

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plin. NH 21.2 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 28.35.3: equitem marcēscere dēsidiā (Lewis & Short)

    Of flowers and leaves that wilt; by a figure, of people who grow slack. Not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short).

  • dēflōrēscō, dēflōrēscere, dēflōruī — drop its blossom; fade, decline

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Catull. 62.43 (Lewis & Short); Col. 2.11, of corn (Lewis & Short)

    Of a plant past its flowering, and by a figure of anything past its best: dēliciae … celeriter dēflōrēscunt (Cic. Cael. 44).

Examples

  • Color tunicae lavandō ēvānuit.

    The shirt’s colour has faded in the wash.composed

See also disappear, colour, light.

SourcesLewis & Short: evanesco · Lewis & Short: pallesco · Lewis & Short: marcesco · Lewis & Short: defloresco
